title: Healthy Fluffy Japanese Tiger Prawn Inarizushi
description: A light and fluffy Japanese-inspired inarizushi featuring tiger prawns, crisp tofu skins, and a tangy vinaigrette. Perfect for a quick low-calorie lunch that feels like a treat.
instructions: Rinse the tiger prawns and pat them dry with a paper towel.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat and cook the prawns 2 to 3 minutes per side until opaque, then set aside to cool.

In a saucepan, combine the rice with 180ml water, soy sauce, mirin, rice vinegar, and sugar, bring to a boil, then simmer until the water is absorbed, about 15 minutes, and fluff the rice before letting it cool.
While the rice cools, julienne the cucumber, grate the daikon radish, and mince the garlic.
Fry each tofu skin pouch in a dry pan over medium heat until crisp, then cut them to the desired size.
Fill each tofu pouch with a scoop of cooked rice, a spoonful of cucumber, a spoonful of daikon, and a prawn, then press gently to seal.
Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds over the assembled inarizushi.
Drizzle the remaining soy sauce over the sushi or squeeze lime juice for added brightness.
Place the sushi in the refrigerator for 10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld before serving.
Serve cold or at room temperature, optionally accompanied by a light cucumber soup.
